key_insight: Clifford disentanglers can reduce entanglement in molecular electronic structure states without destroying Pauli-string Hamiltonian structure, making simulations more efficient.
engineering_relevance: This gives tensor-network and quantum algorithms a structure-preserving preprocessing tool that can lower bond-dimension needs, reduce sensitivity to orbital ordering/mapping, and improve practical accuracy.
method: Classify Clifford operators by how they change Schmidt spectra across a bipartition.
Shrink the search space to 20 two-qubit and 91,392 four-qubit representatives.
Embed the disentanglers in an iterative Clifford-augmented MPS workflow and also test shallow-circuit VQE.
evidence_signal: Across the molecular test cases studied, the method reduced energy errors at fixed bond dimension and also improved shallow-circuit VQE performance.
watch_item: Benefits depend on the underlying correlation structure, and the Clifford search/selection still adds implementation overhead that may limit scalability.
paper_title: Clifford disentanglers for entanglement reduction in molecular electronic structure simulations
